correctness.rationale: For squarefree \(pq\), the factorization digit count is exactly \(a+b\), while the product has only \(a+b-1\) or \(a+b\) digits. The exact threshold is therefore immediate. The prime number theorem gives uniform scaled prime-block measures, and the area of \(uv\ge B\) in \([1,B]^2\) is \(B(B-1-\log B)\). The diagonal deletion for equal blocks has relative size tending to zero.

evidence: Pinch proves general existence results for squarefree economical and extravagant integers and reports finite global counts.
De Koninck--Luca 2005 prove arbitrarily long consecutive economical strings in every base.
De Koninck--Doyon--Letendre prove a Gaussian central distribution for factorization-digit counts over all integers.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results are broader in ambient integer range but do not dominate the conditioned squarefree-semiprime problem. A global density or Gaussian law does not determine the two-prime digit-block conditional proportion.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Existence of squarefree economical integers does not imply the exact two-prime classification or its limiting block proportion. The prior own semiprime density uses a different divisor-sum predicate and has no implication for digit economy.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected literature treats general economical numbers, consecutive strings, global counting, or central factorization-digit distributions. No inspected source states the squarefree-semiprime exact dichotomy together with the explicit prime-digit-block limiting proportion.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2006 global counting paper was not available in this run; only its abstract was inspected.
Recamán's 1995 problem and some recreational-number discussions are not uniformly available as searchable full text.
A short semiprime observation could exist under the older terms equidigital representation or economical numbers without being indexed as a semiprime result.

value.rationale: Squarefree semiprimes are the first nontrivial multiplicative layer beyond primes, and digit blocks are intrinsic to equidigitality. The theorem gives a complete local classification and an explicit limiting law rather than a bounded table, linking a classical digit-factorization notion to prime-number asymptotics.
